title: Frittata di Zucchine
subtitle: Italian omelette with courgette
excerpt: Frittata di zucchine is an Italian open omelette made with eggs, courgette, and parmesan. It is cooked slowly on the hob and finished under the grill rather than folded. The result is set and firm all the way through, not runny like a French omelette. It is good hot, warm, or at room temperature.
sourceNotes: The frittata is the standard Italian preparation for eggs cooked with vegetables or other fillings. It differs from a French omelette in that it is not folded, is cooked all the way through, and is served flat. Frittata di zucchine is one of the most common summer frittate across all regions of Italy.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Frittata is often served at room temperature. Make it up to 2 hours ahead and leave uncovered at room temperature. Do not refrigerate before serving.

glossaryTerms.definition: An Italian omelette cooked slowly and set all the way through rather than folded. The surface is finished under a grill or by flipping.

content.text: is an Italian flat omelette, cooked slowly without folding. This one uses courgette fried until golden, then combined with beaten eggs and parmesan and cooked on the hob until the edges and base are set. The top is finished under the grill rather than flipped. The result is a thick, even disc that cuts into wedges and holds its shape. It is equally good hot, at room temperature, or cold the next day.

Fry the courgette slices in 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a 24 to 26 cm ovenproof frying pan over medium-high heat. Cook for 8 to 10 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden on both sides and soft. Season with salt and pepper. Spread them evenly over the base of the pan.
Beat the eggs in a bowl with the parmesan, a pinch of salt, and black pepper.

Add the remaining tablespoon of olive oil to the pan and lower the heat to medium-low. Pour the egg mixture over the courgette. Cook undisturbed for 8 to 10 minutes until the base and sides are set but the top is still a little loose.
Transfer the pan to the grill and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until the top is just set and lightly golden. It should not brown deeply.
Leave to cool in the pan for 5 minutes. Slide onto a board or plate and cut into wedges.

Frittata is the Italian answer to using up vegetables with eggs. Every region and every household has its own versions. The courgette frittata is particularly common in summer when courgettes are at their peak. It is everyday food: quick, inexpensive, good at any temperature, and equally at home on a lunch table or in a picnic basket.
